sheet-1-1.description: The western and larger part of sheet 1 covers the residential blocks of Pemberton east of the town centre, between Jane Street on the west and Reynolds Street, with a few lots beyond Reynolds, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. From north to south it shows Jarvis Street, Hanover Street (the main road through the borough), Hough Street and Egbert Street, with Odd Fellows Cemetery lettered south of Egbert at the foot of the sheet. Blocks 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 11 are mostly frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories with sheds, autos and stables behind; numbered lots run from the 220s on Jarvis to the 420s on Hanover and Egbert. A short alley runs east from Reynolds between Hanover and Hough. At the east end of Hanover a short piece of street is lettered 'Street (no name)', and the plant of the Pemberton Township Water, Sewerage and Light Company, with its sewage gas plant, stands beside it. Water pipes of 4 inches are marked in Jarvis, Hanover and Hough, with street widths of 30 to 66 feet. A heavy line marks the edge of what the part draws: beyond it the sheet carries the title cartouche, the key, a key map of the town at 600 feet to an inch, the water and fire department notes and the index, all cut out of this part, and a separately placed drawing of the railroad district (part 2). Lettering along the line reads 'No exposure'. The north arrow points to the upper right, so Hanover Street, horizontal on the sheet, runs north-north-east on the ground.
notes: Hanover, Jarvis, Hough, Egbert, Jane and Reynolds are today's Hanover Street, Jarvis Street, Hough Street, Egbert Street, Jane Street and Reynolds Street.
The short street lettered 'Street (no name)' at the east end of Hanover is probably today's St John Street.
Jarvis / Reynolds is a T junction of two 30 ft streets; it was not detected and was hand-picked.

Map, 50 ft. Printed sheet 1; also carries the title cartouche, key, key map of the town (600 ft to an inch) and index in the upper right, cut out of the mask. Two parts: part 1 left of the heavy line (blocks 4-8, 10, 11: Jarvis, Hanover, Hough, Egbert between Jane and Reynolds, Odd Fellows Cemetery at the foot); part 2 lower right (blocks 23-25: Hanover east of the Pemberton and Hightstown Railroad, passenger and freight depots, J.G. Montgomery coal yard, H.D. Harker hay press, Garden States Dairy, Arneys Mount Road and Juliustown Road at the east end), drawn displaced from part 1 at the same scale and orientation.

sheet-1-2.description: The lower right part of sheet 1 is a separately placed drawing of the railroad district at the east end of Pemberton, at 50 feet to an inch and turned about eight degrees from the main part of the sheet. It shows Hanover Street east of the town, lots 501 to 526, where it crosses the tracks of the Pemberton and Hightstown Railroad and the railroad's driveway, and divides at the right edge into Arneys Mount Road and Juliustown Road. North of Hanover lie the freight depot with its cattle pen, the passenger depot, the coal yard and lumber sheds of J.G. Montgomery Co. Inc. (hardware, coal office, agricultural implements, lime and salt), storage of railroad ties, H.D. Harker's hay pressing and storage barn, a hay and grain store and scales. South of Hanover, blocks 24 and 25 hold a few dwellings, a poultry shipping shed, the Garden States Dairy Co. milk depot with its platform, and an ice house near the foot of the sheet. Several tracks fan out through the yard, and the scale of feet is printed across the bottom margin. Hanover is drawn 57 feet wide at the west end and 50 feet at the fork. The part is bounded on the west and north by heavy lines marked 'No exposure' and by the index box of the sheet.
notes: Hanover east of the railroad district is today's Fort Dix Road (County Route 616), which continues Hanover Street; Juliustown Road is the continuation of Fort Dix Road north of the fork.
Arneys Mount Road is today's Arney's Mount Road (County Route 668).

The Pemberton and Hightstown Railroad is gone; OpenStreetMap keeps it as a razed line (Union Transportation Company) ending at Fort Dix Road, and the old Pennsylvania Railroad line to the west is the Pemberton Trail.

No street junction can be detected on this part; it was placed from the hand-picked Arneys Mount Road fork and a derived point along Hanover Street, a two-point helmert. The razed railroad's end in OpenStreetMap falls within a few metres of where the tracks cross Hanover on the sheet under this placement.

Map, 50 ft. Printed sheet 1; also carries the title cartouche, key, key map of the town (600 ft to an inch) and index in the upper right, cut out of the mask. Two parts: part 1 left of the heavy line (blocks 4-8, 10, 11: Jarvis, Hanover, Hough, Egbert between Jane and Reynolds, Odd Fellows Cemetery at the foot); part 2 lower right (blocks 23-25: Hanover east of the Pemberton and Hightstown Railroad, passenger and freight depots, J.G. Montgomery coal yard, H.D. Harker hay press, Garden States Dairy, Arneys Mount Road and Juliustown Road at the east end), drawn displaced from part 1 at the same scale and orientation.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of Pemberton at 50 feet to an inch: the blocks between Antis Street at the left edge and Jane Street at the right edge, from an alley north of Jarvis Street down to Egbert Street, with Hanover Street, the main street, running across the middle and Pemberton Street and Elizabeth Street crossing it. Along Hanover stand the town's stores and public buildings: the Pemberton Inn and its hotel annex at Elizabeth Street, the post office, the fire department, general merchandise, furniture, drug and paint stores, a tin shop and a carpenter shop. The Pemberton Baptist Church stands on the north side of Hanover in block 3 and the M.E. Church with its parsonage, lodge room and horse sheds at Pemberton Street; a cemetery fills the south-east corner of block 9 by Jane Street. South of Hough Street, the A. and G. Rosbach commercial greenhouses with their hot water heating plant occupy block 10, and the public school stands near Jane Street. Most other buildings are frame dwellings with stables and auto sheds. An alley runs from Hough to Egbert between Elizabeth and Jane, and a driveway runs behind the Hanover frontage. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes are shown in Hanover, Jarvis, Pemberton and Elizabeth Streets, with street widths of 40 to 66 feet. The north arrow points to the upper right; 'Scattered fr. dwgs beyond' is printed above the top alley.
notes: All the named streets keep their names today (Antis Street, Jarvis Street, Pemberton Street, Hanover Street, Elizabeth Street, Jane Street, Hough Street, Egbert Street).

Map, 50 ft. One part: blocks 2, 3, 5, 9, 10, 13, 14, 17 between Antis (left edge) and Jane (right edge), Jarvis to Egbert; Pemberton Inn, post office, Baptist and M.E. churches, cemetery, public school, Rosbach greenhouses.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 covers the west end of Pemberton at 50 feet to an inch, where Hanover Street crosses Rancocas Creek on an iron bridge. East of the creek it shows the blocks between Marys Street and Antis Street at the right edge, from Jarvis Street down to Hough and Egbert Streets, with an alley between Hough and Egbert. On the creek just north of the bridge stand the Ridgeway Bros. grist mill, driven by water wheels, and the water works with its triplex pumps, also run by a water wheel; the mill race branches off the creek beside them. North of Hanover lies a large private property with a dwelling, stables, an ice house, coal house and a private lane and driveway. South of Hanover the part shows Grace Episcopal Church, the parish hall used for moving pictures, the Peoples National Bank, a carpenter shop and a barn, with dwellings along Marys Street and a drive off it. West of the creek, Hanover continues past a garage, a blacksmith shop and an ice house; the land there is marked 'Vacant beyond'. The creek, lettered Rancocas Creek, winds down the left half of the sheet, and block 15 between the creek and Marys holds a row of dwellings and a boat house. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are shown in Hanover and Marys. A heavy diagonal line cuts off the upper left corner, which is a separately placed drawing (part 2).
notes: Marys is today's Mary Street.
Antis / Jarvis at the right edge (Antis drawn 20 ft wide) was not detected and was hand-picked.
Marys is drawn about 30 ft wide against a 50 ft right-of-way today; its junctions were measured as narrow pairs with small residuals.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main (Hanover across Rancocas Creek and the iron bridge, Marys, Antis at the right edge, Hough, Egbert; Ridgeway Bros. grist mill, water works, Grace Episcopal Church, Peoples National Bank); part 2 upper left above the heavy line (Budd Cranberry Co. packing houses, Budd Av and Antis north of Jarvis, private lane), drawn displaced from part 1 at the same scale and orientation.

sheet-3-2.description: The upper left corner of sheet 3, cut off by a heavy line, is a separately placed drawing of the district north of Jarvis Street along Antis Street, at 50 feet to an inch and at the same orientation as the rest of the sheet. Its largest property is the Budd Cranberry Co. packing houses: long frame buildings for storage of empty crates, crate making, sorting and cleaning with fan mills, a stock house and a packing house, with a saw and planing mill seldom in operation; the note records no watchman, operation from September to December, wood stoves, electric light, gasoline engines and no city water or fire appliances. A private lane runs through the property and the area east of it is marked 'Private grounds'. Antis Street runs up the part as a 20 ft street, and Budd Av., 65 feet wide, leaves it to the east between block 22 and block 2, with notes of frame stables beyond. A long storage building stands at the top. The margin note at the upper left reads '43 to Rancocas Creek', giving the distance to the creek. Most of the part is open ground; the dividing line is marked 'Vacant beyond' and 'No exposure'.
notes: Budd Av. is today's Budd Avenue; Antis is Antis Street.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (Antis / Budd Av.) and a derived point along Budd Av., a two-point helmert; the detector's own reading of that junction was excluded because it took the east edge of the 20 ft Antis Street for its centre.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main (Hanover across Rancocas Creek and the iron bridge, Marys, Antis at the right edge, Hough, Egbert; Ridgeway Bros. grist mill, water works, Grace Episcopal Church, Peoples National Bank); part 2 upper left above the heavy line (Budd Cranberry Co. packing houses, Budd Av and Antis north of Jarvis, private lane), drawn displaced from part 1 at the same scale and orientation.

sheet-4-1.description: The left and upper part of sheet 4 covers the blocks south of Egbert Street along Elizabeth Street, on the south side of Pemberton, at 50 feet to an inch. Elizabeth Street runs down the part from Egbert, 55 feet wide north of a cross street lettered 'Street (no name)' and 45 feet south of it. Block 26 on the west side has a few dwellings and outbuildings and a concrete-block garage near Egbert, with much open ground; block 27 on the east side is a row of two and two and a half story frame dwellings with auto sheds along an alley; blocks 29 and the lot south of the cross street are largely empty. Along the south side of Egbert, block 28 holds a row of dwellings and Pemberton High School, a brick building heated by steam with electric light and a manual training shop. The alley, 30 feet wide, runs south from Egbert and also continues north of it on sheet 2. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in Elizabeth Street. The part is bounded on the right by a heavy line marked 'No exposure', beyond which the sheet carries a separately placed drawing of the Hanover Street and railroad district (part 2), and 'No exposure' is also printed along the left edge.
notes: The cross street lettered 'Street (no name)' is today's Davis Street; Elizabeth and Egbert keep their names.
Placed from three points: Elizabeth / Egbert (detected), Davis / Elizabeth (hand-picked) and the alley at Egbert, carried from sheet 2; an exact three-point fit with no check.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 left and top (Elizabeth south of Egbert to Davis Street, printed 'Street (no name)', blocks 26-29, Pemberton High School on Egbert); part 2 lower right (blocks 18-21: Hampton, Hanover and Magnolia Road at the Pennsylvania Railroad Long Branch Division, South Pemberton passenger station, O'Donnell barrel works, Davis and Early cranberry packing houses, electric light plant).

sheet-4-2.description: The lower right part of sheet 4 is a separately placed drawing of the district south-west of Pemberton's centre around the South Pemberton station of the Pennsylvania Railroad (Long Branch Division), at 50 feet to an inch and turned about eight degrees from the rest of the sheet. Hanover Street runs across it and meets Hampton Street, coming from the north-west, and Magnolia Rd., going off to the south-east, at one crossing; west of the crossing Hanover narrows to 30 feet. Hampton is lined with dwellings in block 19, and a large open block 18 holds the Thos. Early cranberry packing house. East of the crossing, by the tracks, stand the Alfred Davis cranberry packing house, a cranberry sorting and storage house, E. N. and H. O'Donnell's barrel and stock warehouse and barrel factory, and the electric light plant with an oil engine. On the far side of the railroad lie Ridgeway Bros. grain storage, Wm. Lippincott's coal yard and bins, the freight depot with its platform and the South Pemberton passenger station. Dwellings line Magnolia Rd. in blocks 20 and 21. Two-inch and four-inch water pipes are marked in the streets, and the land east of the railroad is marked 'Vacant beyond'. The part is bounded by heavy lines on the left and top.
notes: Hampton is today's West Hampton Street (County Route 530); the drawn crossing of Hanover, Hampton and Magnolia Rd. is today's junction of Hanover Street, West Hampton Street and the Pemberton Bypass.
Magnolia Rd. near Hanover is today's Pemberton Bypass; the modern Magnolia Road meets Hanover Street about 85 m further north-east, close to where the railroad crossed it.
The railroad is abandoned; OpenStreetMap keeps it as the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division.
Placed from one hand-picked junction and a derived point along Hanover Street, a two-point helmert; low confidence.
